title: Indian-Origin Doctor Sentenced to Six Months in Jail for Secretly Recording Women at Ohio Hospital
excerpt: Advait Deshmukh, a former urology resident at ProMedica Toledo Hospital, pleaded guilty to seven counts of voyeurism after hidden cameras were discovered in a staff bathroom.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Advait Deshmukh received six months in jail for secretly recording women at an Ohio hospital.
  • He pleaded guilty to seven counts of voyeurism and one count of tampering with evidence.
  • Hidden cameras were found in a staff bathroom in June 2025, leading to his identification.
  • The University of Toledo terminated his residency following an internal investigation.
  • Deshmukh's case reflects a troubling trend of voyeurism among medical professionals.

The Sentencing

An Indian-origin former medical resident has been sentenced to six months in jail for secretly recording women in a staff bathroom at a major Ohio hospital. Judge Michael Goulding of Lucas County Common Pleas Court sentenced Advait Deshmukh on June 24 to serve six months at the Corrections Center of Northwest Ohio, followed by three years of probation.

https://x.com/timesofindia/status/2079778713034797449

The terms of Deshmukh's community control include mandatory mental health treatment, participation in a sex offender program, and a no-contact order with victims. He will remain on active adult probation until June 2029.

> **"One victim spoke publicly about the impact, describing the experience as "demoralizing and violating."

![Toledo Hospital."**

How the Case Unfolded

Deshmukh was a third-year urology resident employed by the University of Toledo College of Medicine and Life Sciences, completing his training at ProMedica Toledo Hospital. Hidden cameras were discovered in a private staff bathroom area in June 2025. ProMedica's internal police department identified Deshmukh as the suspect on the same day.

The hospital immediately banned him from all ProMedica facilities and cooperated with the Toledo Police Department and the Lucas County Prosecutor's Office throughout the investigation.

"We took immediate steps, including banning that individual from all ProMedica facilities, closely monitoring compliance, and collaborating with the Toledo Police Department to ensure a thorough investigation."

— ProMedica spokesperson

Deshmukh was indicted on January 13, 2026, on 15 counts of voyeurism and one count of tampering with evidence. On May 1, he entered a guilty plea to seven counts of voyeurism and one count of attempted tampering with evidence as part of a plea deal. The remaining charges were dismissed.

Institutional Fallout

The University of Toledo placed Deshmukh on administrative leave on June 5, 2025, pending its own investigation. His residency appointment was not renewed and concluded on June 30, 2025. At the time of his indictment, public licensing records showed his medical license remained active with no disciplinary action — though medical licensing matters are handled separately from criminal proceedings.

It remains unclear how long the cameras had been in place before they were discovered, or how many people may have been recorded. One victim spoke publicly about the impact, describing the experience as "demoralizing and violating."

![Toledo Hospital. He pleaded guilty to seven counts of voyeurism and one count of tampering with evidence at ProMedica Toledo Hospital in Ohio.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/39/Promedica_Toledo_Hospital_Campus%2C_August_2021.jpg/3840px-Promedica_Toledo_Hospital_Campus%2C_August_2021.jpg)

A Pattern of Cases

Deshmukh's case is one of several involving medical professionals caught placing hidden recording devices in hospital facilities in recent years. In Michigan, Dr. Oumair Aejaz, another Indian-origin physician, was sentenced in December 2025 to 35 to 60 years in prison for secretly recording women and children over six years across multiple hospitals and a swim school. Henry Ford Hospital settled a related civil case for $140 million.

Consequences of Voyeurism
›Deshmukh sentenced to six months in jail and three years of probation.
›Mandatory mental health treatment and sex offender program participation required.
›No-contact order with victims imposed.
›Public licensing records show no disciplinary action against Deshmukh.

In New York, Sanjai Syamaprasad, an Indian-origin hospital worker at the Northwell Sleep Disorders Center in Long Island, admitted to secretly recording approximately 13,000 people in restrooms. He received five years of probation without jail time, a sentence that Nassau County District Attorney Anne Donnelly called inadequate.

Legal Proceedings Continue

While Deshmukh's criminal case has concluded with the plea deal and sentencing, civil litigation may follow. Legal experts have noted that hospitals face potential civil exposure when privacy violations occur under their watch, particularly regarding supervision and access controls. Multiple law firms have indicated they are monitoring the case and representing potential victims.
nri_angle: The case has drawn attention in the Indian-American community, raising concerns about the reputational impact of criminal behavior by Indian-origin professionals in the United States.
